clue.text: Byron said that they would each write one ()

definitions.text: Byron said that they would each write one ()

parts.words: Byron said that they would each write one ()
parts.note: at the Villa Diodati in 1816 Byron proposed that each of his guests compose a tale of the supernatural, the contest that produced Frankenstein

explanation.surface: Byron sets his house party a writing challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diodati contest asked each guest for a supernatural tale, the kind told to raise a shiver.

clue.text: Fitzgerald provided this opening for backers

definitions.text: Fitzgerald provided this opening for backers

parts.words: Fitzgerald provided this opening for backers
parts.note: Penelope Fitzgerald wrote a novel titled with this entrance word (The ___ of Angels), and at a racecourse it is also the takings from paying spectators

explanation.surface: A novelist gives investors their entry point.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in a fence or wall is this barrier, and Penelope Fitzgerald's novel is The Gate of Angels.

clue.text: Sea with American sea god

parts.note: the sea is the ocean

explanation.surface: A sea joined by an American marine deity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Titan personified the great river encircling the world, a primordial deity of the waters.

clue.text: The Laird of Monkbarns

parts.note: Jonathan Oldbuck, Laird of Monkbarns, is the collector of old relics who is the title figure of a Walter Scott novel of 1816

explanation.definitionFit: Scott's novel names its hero, Oldbuck of Monkbarns, by his hobby of collecting relics of the past.

clue.text: Joined by Robert Herrick

parts.note: Herrick's poems are mostly addressed 'To' someone, so a title built of TO plus 'get her' would be a Herrick seduction poem, while the whole word means united

explanation.surface: A poet links arms with a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined are united, in company with one another.

clue.text: TI know not where is that Promethean heat / That can thy light 7 (Othello)

definitions.text: TI know not where is that Promethean heat / That can thy light 7 (Othello)

parts.words: TI know not where is that Promethean heat / That can thy light 7 (Othello)
parts.note: Othello, over the sleeping Desdemona, says he cannot find the divine fire that could rekindle her light once he has put it out; the missing word is his verb for rekindle

explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb in Othello's line means to light again, rekindle.

clue.text: How McMurphy carried out his asylum reconnaissance?

definitions.text: How McMurphy carried out his asylum reconnaissance?

parts.words: How McMurphy carried out his asylum reconnaissance?
parts.note: McMurphy is the hero of Ken Kesey's One ___ Over the Cuckoo's Nest, set in a mental hospital, so he took to the air over the 'nest'

explanation.surface: A mental patient scouts out the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Kesey's title says one went through the air over the cuckoo's nest, as a bird scouting from above.

clue.text: Riot Hal sent out of control, for grandson of Charlemagne

indicators.note: letters sent out of control run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A riotous prince runs amok in place of an emperor's heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis the Pious's eldest son was emperor after him, so Charlemagne's grandson; Disraeli also used the name for a novel.

clue.text: Darling place to stay temporarily

parts.note: in Peter Pan the Lost Boys build a little shelter round Wendy Darling when she arrives in Neverland, now the name for a child's playhouse

explanation.surface: A charming spot for a short stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playhouse is named after the little house built for Wendy Darling in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Chekhov offering expected to take off?

definitions.text: Chekhov offering expected to take off?

parts.words: Chekhov offering expected to take off?
parts.note: a play by Chekhov is named after a shore bird, which might be expected to fly, while 'take off' hints at a successful show

explanation.surface: A Chekhov premiere tipped to be a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's 1896 play is named after the white shore bird shot by Treplev.

clue.text: Educated: during the holidays from

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Educated: during the holidays from (4)' reads as cut short; no parse of the printed words gives ETON

clue.text: Yeats work could make Donne to cry so… (26,4)

indicators.note: the words given could be made into something else by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Rearranging a metaphysical poet's tears could yield an Irish poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 14-down, which comments on this rearrangement; (26,4) is the cross-reference to that run-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats's short 1910 poem about Maud Gonne compares her to Helen.

clue.text: Article on unknown writer

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a writer nobody can name.
explanation.definitionFit: An unattributed work is credited to an anonymous author, abbreviated in this way.

clue.text: Acting as Powell's kings

definitions.meaning: acting as a stand-in, holding a post for the time being
Anthony Powell's novel in A Dance to the Music of Time is ___ Kings

explanation.definitionFit: An acting head holds office only for the time being, and Powell's eleventh Dance volume is titled Temporary Kings.

clue.text: … a new editor could make such a difference!

definitions.text: … a new editor could make such a difference!

parts.words: … a new editor could make such a difference!
parts.note: running on from 11-down, an editor who rearranged the poet's words would be making a textual alteration

explanation.surface: A fresh editor transforms a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A textual correction made by an editor alters the reading of a text.

clue.text: A follower of Olivier — an artist in his own right

definitions.text: A follower of Olivier — an artist in his own right

parts.words: A follower of Olivier — an artist in his own right
parts.note: the surname that follows the first name Olivier belongs to the French composer, not a disciple of the actor Laurence Olivier

explanation.surface: A protégé of the great actor proves a talent himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The French composer's first name was Olivier, so his surname comes after it.

clue.text: Most senior judge from Hermiston swindle is an odd sort

parts.note: Adam Weir, Lord Justice-Clerk, is the hanging judge of Stevenson's Weir of Hermiston
a do is a swindle or con

explanation.surface: A top judge's fraud reveals a strange character.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person is a strange one, an oddball.

clue.text: Scheherazade's prince, offering dates?

parts.note: in the Arabian Nights three princes disguised as wandering dervishes, called Kalandars, tell their tales; the same spelling as a sheet of days

explanation.surface: An Arabian Nights prince serving dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A table of days and months offers dates, and the Arabian Nights' dervish princes bear a homophonous title.

clue.text: Niobe wept for his wife's siblings

definitions.text: Niobe wept for his wife's siblings

parts.words: Niobe wept for his wife's siblings
parts.note: Chloris, the only child of Niobe to survive Apollo and Artemis, married the king of Pylos, father of Nestor

explanation.surface: A grieving mother mourns her children.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Pylos married Chloris, whose brothers and sisters Niobe mourned.

clue.text: Some literature in the post?

definitions.meaning: the world of ... is literature, as in a man of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Literature is called letters, and mailed correspondence consists of letters.

clue.text: Early victim of a master of suspense

definitions.text: Early victim of a master of suspense

parts.words: Early victim of a master of suspense
parts.note: not a Hitchcock film victim but the courtier of ancient Syracuse made to dine beneath a sword hung by a single hair

explanation.surface: Someone killed off early in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Dionysius of Syracuse literally held a sword in suspension over the flatterer at his banquet.

clue.text: Attractive German singer from Koblenz

parts.note: the siren of the Rhine rock upstream of Koblenz, whose song lured boatmen to their deaths

explanation.surface: A glamorous vocalist hails from a Rhine city.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places this Rhine siren on a rock near Koblenz, luring sailors with her song.

clue.text: What Egan supplied to the adventures of Tom and Jerry

definitions.text: What Egan supplied to the adventures of Tom and Jerry

parts.words: What Egan supplied to the adventures of Tom and Jerry
parts.note: Pierce Egan's Regency Life in London followed Tom and Jerry, and in 1828 he wrote a concluding volume to their adventures

explanation.surface: A writer contributes to a cartoon cat and mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Egan's 1828 sequel was titled as the ending of the Tom and Jerry adventures.

clue.text: The following biography of Updike (54)

parts.note: after means following
a life is a biography

explanation.surface: The next life story of an American novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Updike stands for his collection The Afterlife and Other Stories; (54) is a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: John Updike's 1994 story collection bears the title of existence beyond death.

clue.text: Obscure as Inge's landing

definitions.meaning: obscure means unlit, hard to see
William Inge's play The ___ at the Top of the Stairs places it on the landing

explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means shadowy, and Inge's play is The Dark at the Top of the Stairs.

clue.text: Forster character in stab a storyteller might take

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Forster character in stab a storyteller might take' has no count and no parse giving PALE; likely cut short
annotationWithheld.clue: Forster character in stab a storyteller might take

clue.text: Devious Enid Cade's nemesis

indicators.note: devious means crooked, taking a winding route, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: A scheming woman is a rebel's undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 2 the rebel Jack Cade is killed in a Kentish garden by the squire Alexander Iden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentish squire in Henry VI Part 2 slays the rebel Jack Cade.

clue.text: Drudge offers burnt leftovers to Ms Fitzgerald

parts.note: cinder is what remains of burnt coal
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A skivvy hands charred scraps to a jazz singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairytale heroine is the household skivvy of her stepfamily, so her name means a drudge.

clue.text: He wrote many long years ago

definitions.text: He wrote many long years ago

parts.words: He wrote many long years ago
parts.note: Ogden, the American light versifier, published a 1945 collection called Many Long Years Ago

explanation.surface: An author who was writing long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden of that surname wrote the verse collection Many Long Years Ago.

clue.text: Fruit mature in Coppard's work

parts.note: cherry is a fruit
ripe means mature

explanation.surface: Ready fruit appears in a writer's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Coppard's short story and the old street cry share this title.
